first.text: Catching up the Ridge diary for the opening woodland outing. I followed the north fork correctly this time and found that the climb comes much earlier in the lap than I remembered. The first lap felt rushed because I tried to stay with another runner all the way to the gate. On the second I let them go and finished feeling much more settled. For the next long outing, start on my own and use the gate as a reminder to check effort, not as a target time. The watch paused under the trees, so its average pace is not a useful comparison with my previous run. Keep the route and how the two laps felt in the log. I also liked having a few quiet minutes at the end before heading home.

second.text: Ridge finish reflection: starting calmly on the first climb helped. For the next training block, keep those woodland laps but practise the long descent earlier in the cycle.
